title: The Doolittle Raid
subtitle: North Pacific · 2–25 April 1942
tz: Task Force 16 time · UTC+10 (Tokyo one hour behind)
footnote: Task Force 16's clocks on 18 April (Zone −10, UTC+10; Tokyo one hour behind). The rendezvous at 38°N 180°, Hornet's 08:00 fix and Doolittle's launch point are from the Hornet, Enterprise and Doolittle reports; the passage from Alameda and Pearl, the refuelling position and the pickets' stations are reconstructed. The bombers are drawn as one flight to Tokyo and on to Chuchow. Formation members are spread slightly so they don't overlap.

tf18.name: Lieutenant Colonel James H. Doolittle
tf18.role: Commander, Army Air Forces special project — Hornet under Captain Marc Mitscher
tf18.bio: A racing pilot and aeronautical engineer who trained 24 crews to lift a medium bomber off 467 feet of deck. Took off first, ten hours early and 170 miles farther out than planned, bombed Tokyo at noon and bailed out over China in the dark. Sixteen bombers for the loss of seven men and the Japanese Navy's peace of mind.
tf18.fate: Medal of Honor; general; died 1993 aged 96.

tf16.name: Vice Admiral William F. Halsey
tf16.bio: Took two of the Pacific Fleet's four carriers to within 650 miles of Japan. When Nitto Maru's report went out he launched the bombers at once and ran — 'Launch planes. To Col. Doolittle and gallant command, good luck and God bless you'.

nagumo.name: Vice Admiral Chūichi Nagumo
nagumo.bio: Homeward from Ceylon with three carriers when the raid came; ordered east through the Luzon Strait and never within a thousand miles of Halsey.

ships.name: USS Hornet
ships.type: Fleet carrier (Mitscher) — sixteen B-25s on deck

strikes.name: Doolittle's sixteen B-25s
strikes.note: Ten aircraft for Tokyo, two for Yokohama, one each for Yokosuka, Nagoya, Kobe and Osaka; bombs from 1,500 feet at noon, Tokyo time. Then 1,200 miles to China at dusk in rain: fifteen crews bail out or crash-land in Zhejiang; three men killed, eight captured (three executed, one dead in captivity)

strikes.name: York's aircraft to Vladivostok
strikes.note: Captain Edward York, short of fuel, lands at Vozdvizhenka north of Vladivostok; his crew is interned for a year before 'escaping' into Iran

strikes.name: Enterprise dawn search
strikes.note: An SBD sights a patrol boat at 05:58 and drops a message on Enterprise's deck: 'believed seen by enemy'

strikes.name: Enterprise strikes the picket line
strikes.note: Dauntlesses and Wildcats bomb and strafe the picket boats through the afternoon; one SBD ditches, its crew picked up by Nashville

strikes.name: Kisarazu's search
strikes.note: 29 torpedo bombers and 24 fighters of the 26th Air Flotilla search 200 miles out for carriers that are 650 miles away and already running east

engagements.note: 915 rounds of 6-inch at a 90-ton boat pitching in the swell

events: Refuelling done; oilers and destroyers left behind

Doolittle takes off — 467 feet of deck
Last B-25 airborne; Halsey turns for home
Yokosuka: McElroy's bomb hits the carrier Ryūhō in dock
Doolittle bails out near Tien Mu Shan, 70 miles north of Chuchow
Fifteen crews down in Zhejiang; Hallmark's and Farrow's crews will be captured
York lands in the Soviet Union
Nagumo's carriers sent east from the Luzon Strait — too late
